findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: factreason_create_key, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Private data: factreason_package_upgrade_advisory, factreason_create_key, factreason_create_topup_link, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Public sink: factreason_discover_api, factreason_create_key, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Destructive: factreason_package_upgrade_advisory, factreason_api_schema.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: factreason_create_key, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Private data: factreason_package_upgrade_advisory, factreason_create_key, factreason_create_topup_link, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Public sink: factreason_discover_api, factreason_create_key, factreason_subscribe_spec_changes · Destructive: factreason_package_upgrade_advisory, factreason_api_schema

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
